newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN EXOTICS - Beleaguered ringgit tests new low.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN EXOTICS - Beleaguered ringgit tests new low.

text.p: The Malaysian ringgit continued its slide on Friday, breaking through the 2.5100/dollar support level as heavy stop-loss sales were triggered in early trade.
The ringgit tested a new five-month low of 2.5110 to the dollar, where it met some buying interest. It was quoted at 2.5089/99 to the dollar at 0420 GMT against 2.5070/77 on Thursday.
"The market is playing catch up. The big dollar is going higher so ringgit is dragged down," said the head of regional currencies at a European bank in Singapore.
He said the ringgit was the only regional currency moving so sharply, as high interest rates on other units like the baht and rupiah made it worthwhile to carry them.

"Apparently once the 2.5080 level broke last night, people were trying to cut their positions," said a Singapore-based dealer, adding that the selling had subsided and the ringgit was likely to trade between 2.5080-2.5110 for the rest of the day.
"I think (Malaysian) interest rates have peaked. So dollar/ringgit should be bought on dips and eventually see 2.5190," she added.

"Many dealers were predicting the ringgit will strengthen substantially by the year-end, but with this fall, those who don't have the stamina are cutting their losses," said the head of spot foreign exchange dealing at a Malaysian bank.
In Thailand, the baht came under pressure from the dollar's bullish tone against the major currencies as players continued to await the naming of a new Thai premier.
The baht was quoted at 25.415-25.418 to the dollar at 0420 GMT from 25.406-25.409 late on Thursday.
"Baht's weakness followed the U.S. unit's stronger tone against majors. It has nothing to do with economic figures released by the central bank yesterday," said a Bangkok dealer.
The Bank of Thailand on Thursday released key economic data showing Thai exports rose a mere 2.9 percent year-on-year during January-July against 26.5 percent growth in the same period last year.
"The political situation with the prime minister and cabinet ministers is still very uncertain. We should see the dollar/baht higher to 25.43," said a European bank dealer in Singapore.
The Indonesian rupiah held steady as an expected liquidity squeeze in domestic money markets failed to materialise, sending short-dated swap rates down sharply from Thursday's levels.
"The liquidity condition wasn't as tight as operators had anticipated. People who sold on Thursday can cover back now at a much lower level," a Japanese bank dealer in Jakarta said.
Spot rupiah was quoted at 2,318.80/9.80 at 0420 GMT against an opening of 2,318.5/19.5.
A European bank dealer said the dollar's slight rebound could be due to the relatively ample rupiah supply and some short-covering ahead of the weekend.
A U.S. bank dealer said offshore operators were still cautious over the ongoing political dispute centred on ousted opposition leader Megawati Sukarnoputri.
A local authority extended a deadline for Megawati to close her party office to Friday, but there was no hint of an easing in government hostility towards her political activities.
But many operators seemed to expect a smooth settlement of the dispute, as reflected by the relatively stable dollar-rupiah rate in the morning.
- Madhav Reddy in Kuala Lumpur (603-230 8911), Mantik Kusjanto in Jakarta (6221-384-6364), Anuchit Nguyen in Bangkok (662-652-0642) and Sonali Desai in Singapore (65-8703092)
